entrypoints.summary: An operator calls StakedAsset.transferFrom(from, to, value) using a token owner's pre-existing ERC-20 approval; the report's scenario requires unrestricted from and to addresses while the operator has been restricted.

affected_components.role: Vulnerable override applies nonRestricted to from and to and then calls super.transferFrom.

code_slices.fixed: The report recommends adding nonRestricted(msg.sender) to the transferFrom modifier list and states this was fixed in commit d04a30df.
code_slices.surrounding_context: The report locates the vulnerable override at StakedAsset.sol#L294-L302 and explains that the inherited path uses prior approvals.
code_slices.vulnerable: transferFrom is guarded by nonRestricted(from) and nonRestricted(to), then returns super.transferFrom(from, to, value).

negative_controls: A caller restriction check for msg.sender should reject the same restricted operator.
Restricting either from or to is described as causing the existing endpoint checks to apply.
observability.positive_marker: Tokens approved by the user are moved through transferFrom despite the operator being restricted.

preconditions: The operator holds a user-granted ERC-20 approval.
The operator is later added to the restriction list.
The selected from and to addresses are unrestricted.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: transferFrom(from, to, value) where value is within the pre-existing allowance and from/to pass nonRestricted checks.
trigger_steps.summary: The restricted approved operator invokes transferFrom with the approved user's address as from and an unrestricted destination as to.

capabilities.concept: Restricted operator executes delegated token transfer

impacts.concept: Drain of tokens covered by approved allowance

mitigations.concept: Caller restriction check in delegated transfer

relation_candidates.dst: Restricted operator executes delegated token transfer
relation_candidates.rationale: The report states that an operator with a prior approval can continue invoking transferFrom after being restricted because the caller is not checked.
relation_candidates.src: Pre-existing ERC-20 allowance held by a subsequently restricted operator

relation_candidates.rationale: The transferFrom override delegates to the inherited ERC-20 path while omitting a nonRestricted check for msg.sender.
relation_candidates.src: Restricted operator executes delegated token transfer

relation_candidates.dst: Drain of tokens covered by approved allowance
relation_candidates.rationale: The report describes restricted malicious operators draining approved user tokens by selecting unrestricted destinations.

relation_candidates.dst: Caller restriction check in delegated transfer
relation_candidates.rationale: The recommended nonRestricted(msg.sender) check prevents restricted operators from executing transfers even when approvals exist.
relation_candidates.src: Restricted operator executes delegated token transfer

sources.concept: Pre-existing ERC-20 allowance held by a subsequently restricted operator

impact.affected_asset: User ERC-20 tokens held in StakedAsset balances and covered by the operator's allowance.
impact.attacker_capability: A later-restricted operator with a pre-existing user approval can execute delegated transfers to unrestricted destinations.
impact.security_effect: Unauthorized movement of approved user tokens after the approved operator is restricted.

causal_trace.summary: A malicious operator previously obtains a user's ERC-20 approval and is later placed on the restriction list.
The StakedAsset.transferFrom override applies nonRestricted to from and to but omits msg.sender, so restriction enforcement does not cover the operator consuming the allowance.
The override delegates to super.transferFrom, allowing the inherited ERC-20 path to use the existing approval and move tokens despite the operator's restricted status.
A restricted malicious operator can drain tokens covered by legacy approvals to unrestricted destination addresses.

failure.operation: Delegated ERC-20 transferFrom spends an existing allowance after the operator has been restricted.

primary_invariant.kind: restriction coverage for delegated token transfer
primary_invariant.statement: Every participant authorized to execute a delegated transfer, including the allowance-consuming operator, must be unrestricted.
primary_invariant.violated_because: transferFrom checks only the token owner and recipient, leaving msg.sender outside the nonRestricted checks before calling the inherited transferFrom implementation.

quality.review_notes: The public audit report contains the vulnerable override, a bounded attack scenario, a recommended caller check, and a statement that Spearbit verified Tenbin's fix. No upstream repository, resolved commit d04a30df patch, regression test, transaction trace, or executable PoC is present; the reported fix has not been independently code-reviewed in this record.

remediation.invariant_restored: transferFrom additionally applies nonRestricted(msg.sender), preventing a restricted operator from exercising existing approvals.

state_context.attacker_state_setup: The attacker must have obtained user approval before restriction, and the source and destination addresses must remain unrestricted for the reported override checks to pass.
data_structure_invariants: A restriction list must cover the caller that exercises a delegated allowance.
A pre-existing allowance must not remain exercisable by an operator after that operator is restricted.
state_context.state_machine: User grants an operator allowance; the operator is subsequently restricted; it attempts delegated transfer using that pre-existing allowance.

affected_versions_or_commits.value: Audited implementation containing StakedAsset.sol#L294-L302; the report states the finding was fixed in commit d04a30df, but the patch itself is not supplied.
